author: TEDx Talks
description:
Nearly three billion birds have disappeared from North America in the past fifty years. The data is overwhelming, and somehow it isn't moving us fast enough. Pippin Frisbie-Calder has spent her career asking why we struggle to act on what we already know, and what art can do about it. Working at the intersection of printmaking, ecological science, and advocacy, she uses large-scale installations and collaborations with researchers to transform statistics about species loss into experiences people can feel. Her talk opens with a sound that no longer exists, the call of the extinct Ivory-billed Woodpecker, and builds a case for art as one of the most underused tools in the climate response.

Pippin Frisbie-Calder is a visual artist and environmental printmaker based in Louisiana whose large-scale woodcuts, silkscreen prints, and immersive installations bring the threatened ecosystems of the Gulf South into galleries, classrooms, and public spaces.
